title: Workers in the Constitution of India
author: Editorial Desk
summary: Where the Constitution speaks about freedom of association, fair wages and workers' participation.
body:
The Constitution of India does not contain a long chapter on labour, but it speaks about workers in several important places. Knowing them helps in reading any debate on labour law.

## Fundamental Rights

- **Article 19(1)(c)** guarantees all citizens the right to form associations or unions. This is the constitutional base of trade unionism.
- **Article 23** prohibits trafficking and forced labour.
- **Article 24** prohibits employment of children in factories, mines and other hazardous work.

## Directive Principles

The Directive Principles are not enforceable in court, but the Constitution calls them fundamental in the governance of the country. Several relate to workers:

- **Article 39** asks the State to secure adequate means of livelihood, equal pay for equal work for men and women, and protection of workers' health and strength.
- **Article 41** speaks of the right to work and public assistance in unemployment, old age, sickness and disability.
- **Article 42** requires just and humane conditions of work and maternity relief.
- **Article 43** speaks of a living wage and decent conditions of work for workers.
- **Article 43A** (added by the 42nd Amendment) directs the State to take steps to secure the **participation of workers in the management** of industries.

## Labour on the Concurrent List

Labour is a subject on the Concurrent List, so both Parliament and State legislatures can make laws on it. That is why the Labour Codes are central laws that States then support with their own rules.

## Why this matters

When BMS asks for minimum wages, social security or workers' participation, these are not only demands. They connect to the directions that the Constitution itself gives the State.
